title: Loan validation in PL/pgSQL
summary: A stored function with SELECT INTO, FOUND, IF/RETURN and an aggregate check.

tests.name: written in PL/pgSQL
tests.query: SELECT l.lanname FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_language l ON l.oid = p.prolang WHERE p.proname = 'validate_loan';

hints: `SELECT * INTO v_customer FROM customers WHERE customer_id = p_customer_id;` then `IF NOT FOUND THEN RETURN 'NO_CUSTOMER'; END IF;`.
The rules are checked in order and the first one that fails wins. A blocked customer asking for 1 rupee is BLOCKED, not AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE.
A customer with no loans has `sum(amount) = NULL`, and `NULL + amount > limit` is NULL, which IF treats as false. Use `COALESCE(sum(amount), 0)`. Case 9 tests exactly this.
